newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ to hold Japan interest rates low -- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: BOJ to hold Japan interest rates low -- newspaper.

text.p: The director of the Policy Planning Department for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) has said the central bank will maintain its low interest rate policy for the time being, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

In an interview with the the financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun, Takahiro Kawase was also quoted as saying that the Japanese economy is likely be back on its recovery track in the 1997 fiscal year, which begins on April 1.
However, he said the BOJ must monitor economic developments for the time being to make sure that self-sustainable recovery can be achieved.
The BOJ cut the official discount rate by half a percentage point to a historic low of 0.5 percent in September 1995.
"We will keep a watch on economic developments for the time being to make sure that a base for recovery becomes firmer," Kawase said.
Kawase also said it is difficult to pinpoint causes for the recent plunge in Tokyo stock prices.
"What we can say now about share prices is that we will be keeping a close watch on prices to see what messages the market is trying to convey," he said.
